newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut managed care groups plan merger.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut managed care groups plan merger.

text.p: Yale University and Saint Francis Hospital and Medical Center said Wednesday they will merge their managed care plans to create the biggest provider-owned health plan in Connecticut.
The proposed merger of Yale Preferred Health and HealthChoice of Connecticut Inc is subject to approval by the state, the organizations said in a statement.
The merger will allow the combined operation to begin offering a commercial health maintenance organization (HMO) product.
North Haven-based Yale Preferred Health, a licensed HMO founded in April 1995, operates Preferred One Medicaid managed care plan with more than 15,000 members.

Farmington-based HealthChoice, a preferred provider organization (PPO) founded in 1990, covers more than 180,000 lives in the state and includes 6,000 physicians and ancillary providers and 29 hospitals throughout Connecticut.
The merged operation will initially operate under the HealthChoice name, the organizations said.
Financial details of the merger were not announced.
